description: David's 'Atlas is a no-go because I'm booked' was a complete decision. Master acknowledged it but then re-asked whether to close, leave open, or re-date the Monday task, re-litigating a settled question.
correction: When David states a decision, act on its operational consequences without re-asking. A no-go on a task means close it (or mark it per the obvious disposition) and report the action; only ask a follow-up if the decision is genuinely ambiguous about the outcome, not the bookkeeping.
systemic_fix: Apply the 'don't ask unnecessary questions' rule to bookkeeping: decisions imply their file updates. Ask only when the disposition itself is ambiguous, and default to the disposition that matches the words given.
